evidence: Dimension weights: task/tests/scoring.toml [weights] functional = 0.6, polish = 0.2, visual = 0.2, [gates] render/constraints = 0.0, [floors] functional = 0.05; the file is byte-identical to the frozen template (sha256 95f70d6e... both, matching manifest.json:48 and :84) and matches the skill's mandated shaped profile, so real functionality carries 60% and the non-functional dimensions are capped at 0.4 combined. Gate criteria carry weight 1.0 under all_pass aggregation but gates hold no reward mass (score.py:41,46-48 multiplies only [weights]). No weight key appears in any [judge] block. Per-criterion weights in scored/functional/judge.toml (43 binary criteria, total 59.0) are 1.0/1.5/2.0 and track what each proves: 2.0 goes to the hardest, most integrity-critical outcomes (cw_multi_caret_typing_atomic, cw_same_line_carets, cw_js_format_semantics_and_undo, cw_last_good_recovery, cw_stop_cancels_pending_work, cw_live_update_keeps_editing_state); 1.5 to atomic replace, stale-save refusal/draft preservation, preview isolation, dynamic-code refusal, save/reload/restart; 1.0 to basic typing, navigation, basic run, find. Basic typing at 1.0 is not under-weighted in effect because nearly every other functional criterion depends on a working editor. Polish (6 x 1.0) and visual (3 likert x 1.0) are flat, appropriate for peer-level craft checks. Sanity check of maximum non-functional contribution: per-criterion reward share is 0.6/59 = 1.0-2.0% for functional, 3.3% per polish criterion, 6.7% per visual criterion; this per-item disparity is a consequence of the mandated 0.6/0.2/0.2 split spread over broad functional coverage, not a dishonest weight, and the dimension cap keeps a beautiful but barely working app (functional just above the 0.05 floor) at most about 0.43 versus 0.6+ for a fully functional plain app. Measured corroboration on v15 bytes (same golden, same scoring.toml; v16 functional criteria differ, so this is not a v16 score): GPT-5.6-luna reward.json functional 0.4576, polish 1.0, visual 0.5, reward 0.5746 = 0.6*0.4576 + 0.2*1.0 + 0.2*0.5, showing the weights apply as written and functional dominates; Oracle 1.0, nop 0. Adversarial tries: a broken app that is pretty but non-editing must still pass the constraints gate (custom document surface, shared saved record) and exceed the functional floor, and cannot exceed 0.4 from style; a conforming alternative is not penalised by weights because no weight rewards a particular implementation. No v16 configured-judge run exists, but this row's arithmetic is static and fully determined by scoring.toml, judge.toml and score.py, so no required measurement for this row is missing (ranking/discrimination measurement belongs to rows 42/43 and the runtime records).
